RESULT AND INTERPRETATION:

ABL  PML-RARA 
Detected Not-Detected

Comment

  • Acute Promyelocytic Leukemia [APL] accounts for 10–15% of all Acute Myeloid Leukemia [AML] cases. This assay is used for genetic confirmation of APL characterised by the classic translocation t(15;17)(q22;q21) – PML-RARA. It predicts response to all-trans -retinoic acid or arsenic trioxide therapy. It predicts relapse risk, and is used to monitor for minimal residual disease [MRD] postconsolidation therapy. 
  • The assay is reported in the form of a normalized ratio of PML-RARA fusion transcript to the control gene ABL1 expressed as a percentage. 
  • Depending on the location of breakpoint within the PML gene, the following PML-RARA fusion isoforms are detected: Type A (short, S-form, bcr-3), results due to fusion of PML exon 3 with RARA exon 3, and is seen in 30% to 40% of t(15;17)-positive cases. Type B (long, L-form, bcr-1), results due to fusion of PML exon 6 and RARA exon 3, and is seen in 50% to 55% of t(15;17)-positive cases. Type B variant (variable, V-form, bcr-2), results due to fusion of variable portion of PML exon 6 with exon 3 of the RARA gene, and is seen in 5% to 10% of t(15;17)-positive cases 

Limitations 

Bone marrow samples are preferred for maximum sensitivity. Poor RNA yield will lead to false negatives.
